statements.impact_statement: PROVEN false-positive, measured 2026-10-08 on calico-node 3.32.0. The advisory is Wolfi's, keyed to the package calico-node-3.32 3.32.0-r4 (fixed in 3.32.2-r3, a revision not in the public APKINDEX on 2026-10-08), and its vulnerable code is the Go module github.com/gopacket/gopacket linked into that package's Go binaries. Listing every ELF file of calico-node-3.32-3.32.0-r4.apk and checking each for Go build info showed exactly two Go binaries, /usr/bin/calico-node and /usr/bin/mountns; the rest are the C BIRD daemons and BPF objects in /usr/lib/calico/bpf. This image replaces both binaries with quench-calico-node (melange `replaces: calico-node-3.32`), built from the v3.32.0 tag with the floor pass. Verified by the build itself: melange.yaml runs `go version -m` on both replacement binaries and fails if github.com/gopacket/gopacket is below v1.6.1; and the gate's binary scan of /usr/bin/calico-node (run 37707336807) reported none of these advisories, only cel-go, since floored. The vulnerable github.com/gopacket/gopacket code is therefore not present in the image; only the package record of the replaced apk still carries the version.

PROVEN false-positive, measured 2026-11-10 on calico-node 3.32.0. The advisory is Wolfi's, keyed to the package calico-node-3.32 3.32.0-r4 (fixed in 3.32.3-r1, a revision not in the public APKINDEX; Wolfi stopped publishing calico-3.32 after 2026-06-11), and its vulnerable code is the Go module github.com/gopacket/gopacket below v1.7.2 (GHSA-358w-w75h-x6rx). Listing every ELF file of calico-node-3.32-3.32.0-r4.apk and checking each for Go build info showed exactly two Go binaries, /usr/bin/calico-node and /usr/bin/mountns; the rest are the C BIRD daemons and BPF objects in /usr/lib/calico/bpf. This image replaces both binaries with quench-calico-node (melange `replaces: calico-node-3.32`), built from the v3.32.0 tag with the floor pass. melange.yaml floors gopacket at v1.7.2 and runs `go version -m` on both replacement binaries, failing if gopacket is below v1.7.2. The vulnerable gopacket code is therefore not present; only the package record of the replaced apk still carries the version.

PROVEN false-positive, measured 2026-11-10 on calico-node 3.32.0. The advisory is Wolfi's, keyed to the package calico-node-3.32 3.32.0-r4 (fixed in 3.32.3-r2, not in the public APKINDEX), and its vulnerable code is the Go module github.com/klauspost/compress below v1.20.2 (GO-2026-6865, zstd). Listing every ELF file of calico-node-3.32-3.32.0-r4.apk and checking each for Go build info showed exactly two Go binaries, /usr/bin/calico-node and /usr/bin/mountns; the rest are the C BIRD daemons and BPF objects in /usr/lib/calico/bpf. This image replaces both binaries with quench-calico-node (melange `replaces: calico-node-3.32`), built from the v3.32.0 tag with the floor pass. `go version -m` on both binaries of the published image (ghcr.io/quenchworks/images/calico-node:3.32.0, linux/amd64, extracted 2026-11-10) lists no github.com/klauspost/compress at all, and melange.yaml fails the build if a later floor pass links it below v1.20.2. The vulnerable compress code is therefore not present.

Verified 2026-11-18 on the published image ghcr.io/quenchworks/images/calico-node:3.32.0 (sha256:9b3be360c9b6...). The advisory is CVE-2026-128085 in go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk below 1.47.0, matched here through Wolfi's package-level secdb entry for calico-node-3.32 (fixed in 3.32.4-r1, a revision the public APKINDEX does not carry; it tops out at 3.32.0-r4). This image does not ship Wolfi's Go binaries: quench-calico-node rebuilds them from the 3.32.0 tag with the house floor, which includes go.opentelemetry.io/otel/sdk@v1.47.0 (apps/calico-node/melange.yaml FLOOR). go version -m over every executable in the extracted image finds exactly one that links OpenTelemetry, /usr/bin/calico-node, at go.opentelemetry.io/otel@v1.47.0 with no older otel/sdk module; no other binary links otel at all. The vulnerable code below 1.47.0 is therefore not present. Revisit if the overlay stops replacing a Go binary from the Wolfi package.
